vision.title: The Box That Felt Small

inputs.title: The Box That Felt Small
inputs.logline: After Jenny hides the shame of misreading a word, Patch leads the Box Monsters into a shoebox classroom where a giant mistake must become something she can try again with, not something that makes her small.

orderedEvents.text: Jenny stands at the front of the classroom holding her worksheet.
The word BRIDGE is written on the board.
Jenny looks at the word. Her fingers tighten around the paper.
One child lets out a tiny laugh. Another child laughs because the first one did.
Jenny looks at the word again. It feels much bigger now.
Final Frame: Jenny frozen, embarrassed, holding the worksheet close.

beats.storyBeat: Jenny stands in the exposed classroom space and tries to read the line. The ordinary word on the board becomes dangerous through silence, hesitation and the accidental wrong word. The tiny laugh is not cruelly staged, but it is enough to make Jenny’s body close around the worksheet and make her corrected answer come out small.
beats.want: Jenny wants to read the sentence correctly and get safely through her turn.
beats.need: She needs to know that a visible mistake does not reduce her worth.
beats.kidRead: It feels awful when you say something wrong and everyone hears it.
beats.adultRead: A small public stumble can become disproportionately huge inside a sensitive child, even when the adults respond gently.
beats.emotionalIntent: Let the audience feel the blush before the magic begins: embarrassment as a physical freeze, not a lesson.

She slips the folded worksheet into her school bag.
Final Frame: Jenny holding her bag, the folded worksheet hidden inside.

beats.storyBeat: Back at her desk, Jenny is no longer at the front of the room, but the feeling has stayed in front of her. She folds the worksheet smaller and answers a kind check-in with a tiny false assurance, choosing concealment over connection before the school bell releases her with the shame hidden in her bag.
beats.want: Jenny wants the moment to be over and for nobody to look closely at her hurt.
beats.need: She needs permission to admit she is not all right without becoming the mistake.
beats.kidRead: Even after class moves on, your stomach can still feel stuck in the bad moment.
beats.adultRead: The polite ‘I’m fine’ masks the real emotional event: Jenny is beginning to hide rather than process the shame.
beats.emotionalIntent: Keep this quiet and recognisable; the drama is in the mismatch between Jenny’s nod and the truth of her posture.

orderedEvents.text: Shot 03: The Feeling Goes Into The Box
Jenny kneels on her bedroom floor.
Her decorated shoebox sits beside her bed. It has stars, hearts and one wonky rainbow drawn on the lid.
Inside are small treasures: a ribbon, a pebble, an old badge, a folded card.
She places the folded worksheet inside the box.
For a moment, she keeps her hand on it.

orderedEvents.speaker: Jenny
orderedEvents.text: I don’t want to think about it.
The box gives the smallest cardboard sigh.
Final Frame: The closed shoebox on the bedroom floor.

beats.storyBeat: In her bedroom, Jenny brings the folded worksheet to her decorated shoebox, a safe place for treasured things. She tries to make the feeling disappear by placing it inside and closing the lid, not noticing that the box has received more than paper: it has received the feeling she cannot carry alone.
beats.want: Jenny wants to put the worksheet away and stop thinking about the classroom mistake.
beats.need: She needs the hidden feeling to be met, not buried.
beats.kidRead: Jenny hides the paper because looking at it hurts.
beats.adultRead: The shoebox becomes a child’s private emotional container: a tender coping strategy that also signals isolation.
beats.emotionalIntent: Make the action intimate and gentle, with the box feeling like a confidant even before the magic answers.

beats.storyBeat: Later, with Jenny asleep, the shoebox quietly opens just enough to send a warm golden signal through the dark. The folded worksheet trembles, and the room’s silence becomes a secret request for help moving from Jenny’s world toward The Fold.
beats.want: The shoebox wants to send the feeling call without waking Jenny.
beats.need: The hidden shame needs a safe responder.
beats.kidRead: The box knows Jenny needs help even though she is asleep.
beats.adultRead: The fantasy externalises emotional processing: care begins when the child is no longer consciously defending against the feeling.
beats.emotionalIntent: Shift from private sadness to wonder; this is the promise that hidden feelings are not abandoned.

beats.storyBeat: The Fold receives the call in the middle of Patch and Nib’s wobbly routine, turning comic imbalance into mission focus. The signal honk collapses Patch’s tower-of-calm act, but when Tilly reads the feeling as shame, the team’s stillness shows they understand the delicacy of what they are entering.
beats.want: The monsters want to identify the call and know where to go.
beats.need: They need to treat shame with care rather than with noise or bravado.
beats.kidRead: The funny cardboard city gets an alarm, and the monsters discover the feeling is serious.
beats.adultRead: The scene balances levity with respect: shame changes the team’s body language before anyone explains why it matters.
beats.emotionalIntent: Use comedy as an entry ramp, then let the word shame quiet the room.

beats.need: Patch needs to turn courage into patience, not just speed.
beats.kidRead: The monsters are off on the rescue, even if they are a bit ridiculous about it.
beats.adultRead: Patch’s leadership is aspirational: he knows the correct emotional approach before he has fully learned how to practice it.
beats.emotionalIntent: Build momentum without losing tenderness; the tunnel should feel like a handmade passage into Jenny’s inner life.

beats.need: They need to see that the problem is not the word itself but Jenny’s relationship to the moment.

beats.adultRead: Shame magnifies a single error until the whole environment seems organised around it.
beats.emotionalIntent: Make the world funny but not silly at Jenny’s expense; the scale of the word should feel both ridiculous and painful.

beats.adultRead: The repair begins with attunement: distance, lowered posture, self-disclosure and non-demanding presence.

beats.storyBeat: The shame world tightens as the walls fold inward and the repeated word gets louder. Rumble physically holds space as best he can while Patch kneels by Jenny’s echo and names the fear beneath the mistake: feeling like everyone can see it. Then he separates the mistake from Jenny’s size, and the room pauses long enough for Tilly to understand what has to change.

beats.need: Jenny’s echo needs someone to name the feeling accurately and contradict its false meaning.
beats.kidRead: The walls squeeze in until Patch says the true thing that makes them stop.
beats.adultRead: The low point resolves not through force but through language matched to embodied shame: being seen is not the same as being diminished.
beats.emotionalIntent: Make this the emotional hinge; danger outside and tenderness inside must happen at the same time.

beats.storyBeat: Tilly accepts the lesson and transforms the Correct Answer Machine into a Try Again Machine. Patch turns the handle, and a golden card gives Jenny’s echo the truth of the episode. She stands taller, the classroom warms, BRIGGLE becomes BRIDGE, and the repair light rises out of the shoebox world toward Jenny’s real life.

beats.need: Jenny’s echo needs a new meaning for the mistake: not fixed forever, but safe enough to try again.
beats.kidRead: The machine changes jobs and gives Jenny a golden message that helps the scary word become normal again.
beats.adultRead: The solution shifts from outcome to process; resilience is framed as returning to the task with dignity intact.
beats.emotionalIntent: Make the repair feel handmade and earned, not magically convenient: the same machine works only after its purpose changes.

beats.storyBeat: Morning brings Jenny back to the shoebox, where the worksheet is repaired with golden tape and the card waits beside it. She reads the message with confusion before a small smile arrives. Most importantly, she pockets the card and holds the worksheet without folding it smaller, showing the internal repair through action.
beats.want: Jenny wants to understand what has happened to her worksheet and card.
beats.need: She needs to carry the truth into the day physically, not just hear it once.
beats.kidRead: Jenny finds the magic helped her paper, and she feels a bit braver.
beats.adultRead: The behavioural payoff is subtle: the worksheet remains visible and uncrushed, evidence that shame no longer dictates her hands.
beats.emotionalIntent: Keep the magic secret and quiet; Jenny should not become suddenly fearless, only a little more able.

beats.storyBeat: Back in the classroom, Jenny faces the same word and accepts the chance to read one line. She is still nervous, but she stays, says the sentence, and then gently adds the old mistaken word herself. The children’s laughter is kind this time because Jenny is part of it. The shoebox twitches, The Fold glows, Nib’s distant voice keeps the cafe joke alive, and Jenny’s smile carries the secret repair into warm black.
beats.want: Jenny wants to try the line again without being swallowed by the old embarrassment.
beats.need: She needs to discover that courage can include nervousness and even a remembered mistake.
beats.kidRead: Jenny says the word right, makes her own little joke, and the magic friends are secretly happy.
beats.adultRead: The healing is not amnesia; Jenny integrates the embarrassing moment by choosing when and how to mention it.
beats.emotionalIntent: End on modest triumph rather than applause: the final feeling is private confidence, shared kindness and a tiny hidden wink from The Fold.

direction.premise: A classroom reading mistake follows Jenny home until her shoebox calls the Box Monsters into a handmade shame world built around one too-large wrong word.
direction.dramaticQuestion: Can the monsters help Jenny carry the mistake differently before shame makes her feel too small to try again?
direction.theme: Getting something wrong does not make you small.
direction.externalJourney: Jenny misreads a word, hides the worksheet in her shoebox, and the monsters travel from The Fold into a cardboard classroom where the mistaken word has swollen into the room’s bossy centrepiece. Their attempted fix fails, then they transform the machine and the meaning of the mistake so Jenny can face the word again.
direction.internalJourney: Jenny moves from public embarrassment, to hiding, to a tiny private openness, to reclaiming the mistake with humour, and finally to trying again while still feeling nervous.
direction.relationshipChanges: Patch begins as a brave responder who wants to help quickly, but earns Jenny’s echo’s trust by sitting with her instead of fixing her. Tilly shifts from controlling the outcome to redesigning her solution around emotional truth. Rumble protects space rather than forcing confidence. Nib’s odd humour becomes the safe bridge between shame and self-acceptance.
direction.emotionalCurve: Quiet pressure builds into embarrassment, then withdrawal, then magical concern. The middle tightens as the wrong fix makes shame heavier. Relief arrives first through being met gently, then through laughter that belongs to Jenny rather than at Jenny. The ending lands in soft courage and secret warmth.
direction.comedyCurve: The comedy starts as character imbalance in The Fold, turns into dry diagnosis and wonky tools, dips during the failed fix, then returns as Nib’s sideways cafe idea makes the mistake feel usable rather than poisonous. The final joke is small, affectionate and earned.
direction.setupPayoffMap: The word BRIDGE becomes BRIGGLE in class, then grows into the shame world’s looming word, then shrinks through laughter, becomes BRIDGE again, and returns in the classroom as a word Jenny can say. Jenny folds the worksheet smaller when ashamed, then later carries it without folding it. The Correct Answer Machine fails, then becomes the Try Again Machine. The shoebox’s first sigh and call pay off as its warm twitch and The Fold lamp glow.
direction.visualMotifs: Folding paper as shrinking self-worth; oversized lettering as shame taking up too much space; golden tape and cards as repair, not erasure; cardboard walls pressing inward and later opening with warmth; the shoebox as a private container that becomes a gentle doorway.

vision.premise: A classroom reading mistake follows Jenny home until her shoebox calls the Box Monsters into a handmade shame world built around one too-large wrong word.
vision.dramaticQuestion: Can the monsters help Jenny carry the mistake differently before shame makes her feel too small to try again?
vision.theme: Getting something wrong does not make you small.
vision.externalJourney: Jenny misreads a word, hides the worksheet in her shoebox, and the monsters travel from The Fold into a cardboard classroom where the mistaken word has swollen into the room’s bossy centrepiece. Their attempted fix fails, then they transform the machine and the meaning of the mistake so Jenny can face the word again.
vision.internalJourney: Jenny moves from public embarrassment, to hiding, to a tiny private openness, to reclaiming the mistake with humour, and finally to trying again while still feeling nervous.
vision.relationshipChanges: Patch begins as a brave responder who wants to help quickly, but earns Jenny’s echo’s trust by sitting with her instead of fixing her. Tilly shifts from controlling the outcome to redesigning her solution around emotional truth. Rumble protects space rather than forcing confidence. Nib’s odd humour becomes the safe bridge between shame and self-acceptance.
vision.emotionalCurve: Quiet pressure builds into embarrassment, then withdrawal, then magical concern. The middle tightens as the wrong fix makes shame heavier. Relief arrives first through being met gently, then through laughter that belongs to Jenny rather than at Jenny. The ending lands in soft courage and secret warmth.
vision.comedyCurve: The comedy starts as character imbalance in The Fold, turns into dry diagnosis and wonky tools, dips during the failed fix, then returns as Nib’s sideways cafe idea makes the mistake feel usable rather than poisonous. The final joke is small, affectionate and earned.

The shoebox’s first sigh and call pay off as its warm twitch and The Fold lamp glow.

northStar.surfaceStory: The Box Monsters enter Jenny’s shoebox shame classroom, where the wrong word BRIGGLE has become huge, loud and bossy, and they must help Jenny’s emotional echo face it without being crushed by it.
northStar.universalTruth: A mistake feels enormous when you think it has become what everyone sees instead of you.
northStar.childClearWant: Jenny wants the loud wrong word to stop pointing at her.
northStar.emotionalNeed: She needs someone to stay near, not laugh, and show that getting a word wrong has not made her small.
northStar.falseBeliefUnderPressure: If I get this wrong, everyone can see only the wrongness, and I shrink inside it.
northStar.relationshipEngine: Patch changes because Jenny’s echo does not respond to fixing; Rumble’s protection shows him the room needs space, Tilly’s machine shows him correctness can hurt, and Nib’s play shows him the mistake can be held lightly.
northStar.ordinaryLifeTruth: When a child is ashamed, the first repair is not the right answer; it is feeling safe enough to try again.
northStar.sceneTurn: The scene turns from defeating BRIGGLE as an error to changing what BRIGGLE means: from evidence against Jenny into something she can play with, then try again from.
audienceJourney: Whoa, that mistake is huge and silly.
Oh no, Jenny’s echo is tiny beside it.
The machine is funny, but it is making things worse.
Rumble holding the room makes the danger feel real.
Patch saying the fear out loud should feel gentle, not teachy.
Nib making BRIGGLE useful lets the audience laugh with the mistake, not at Jenny.
The final repair should feel like a breath returning, not a trophy win.
northStar.finalAfterFeeling: Relief with a small brave lift: Jenny’s shame has not vanished forever, but it is no longer bigger than her.
northStar.dialogueSubtractionOpportunity: Do not add any extra explanation of the lesson. Jenny’s hands loosening, Patch lowering himself, Rumble physically holding space, Tilly stopping the machine, and BRIGGLE shrinking must carry what shame is doing and why the repair works.
northStar.environmentPressure: The classroom is the feeling under pressure: the word repeats, the walls fold inward, furniture behaves embarrassed, the machine clunks certainty, and the board/room scale makes one school moment feel like the whole world.

transformation.entryBelief: If a feeling is frightening, a brave helper should get in fast and make the scary thing stop.
transformation.entryFeeling: Protective urgency mixed with discomfort at how loud and oversized the mistake has become.
transformation.pressureBehaviour: He starts by reacting to BRIGGLE as a problem to manage, then looks to answers and reassurance while the room keeps pressing in.
transformation.costlyChoice: Patch stops trying to beat the word and kneels with Jenny’s echo inside the shame, admitting his own fear of being seen when he gets something wrong.
transformation.exitBelief: Helping is not making the mistake disappear first; helping is making the person feel big enough to meet it again.
transformation.exitAction: He turns the transformed Try Again Machine handle as the room warms and BRIGGLE can become BRIDGE.

tapestry.physicalMotif: The written word as a weight: BRIGGLE begins as a huge accusing object, then becomes a play object, then settles back into BRIDGE; Jenny’s loosening hands are the small human counter-motif.
tapestry.sonicMotif: A repeated, echoing “Briggle” and the machine’s hard “Correct” should feel like shame copying itself; by the end, replace the attack with the softer rhythm of a handle turning and repair light rising.
tapestry.colourAndLightProgression: Begin with flat classroom coolness and cardboard shadow around the board; tighten into dull, close, echo-heavy tones during the machine and folding walls; warm gradually only after BRIGGLE is reclaimed, ending with a gentle golden lift rather than a sudden blaze.
tapestry.thematicVisualContrast: Hard correctness versus safe nearness: the machine, board and giant word stand upright and certain; Patch lowering himself, Rumble holding space, and the group playing café with BRIGGLE make the room less like a test and more like somewhere Jenny can breathe.
tapestry.openingClosingRhyme: Open on a classroom built around one giant wrong word dominating everyone; close on the same classroom warmed and resized, with the word changed back and a golden card carrying the meaning Jenny can take into morning.

inputs.title: The Box That Felt Small
inputs.logline: After Jenny hides the shame of misreading a word, Patch leads the Box Monsters into a shoebox classroom where a giant mistake must become something she can try again with, not something that makes her small.

orderedEvents.text: Jenny stands at the front of the classroom holding her worksheet.
The word BRIDGE is written on the board.
Jenny looks at the word. Her fingers tighten around the paper.
One child lets out a tiny laugh. Another child laughs because the first one did.
Jenny looks at the word again. It feels much bigger now.
Final Frame: Jenny frozen, embarrassed, holding the worksheet close.

beats.storyBeat: Jenny stands in the exposed classroom space and tries to read the line. The ordinary word on the board becomes dangerous through silence, hesitation and the accidental wrong word. The tiny laugh is not cruelly staged, but it is enough to make Jenny’s body close around the worksheet and make her corrected answer come out small.
beats.want: Jenny wants to read the sentence correctly and get safely through her turn.
beats.need: She needs to know that a visible mistake does not reduce her worth.
beats.kidRead: It feels awful when you say something wrong and everyone hears it.
beats.adultRead: A small public stumble can become disproportionately huge inside a sensitive child, even when the adults respond gently.
beats.emotionalIntent: Let the audience feel the blush before the magic begins: embarrassment as a physical freeze, not a lesson.

The word BRIDGE is written on the board.

cuts.speaker: Teacher
cuts.dialogue: Teacher: Take your time, Jenny.

cuts.action: Jenny looks at the word. Her fingers tighten around the paper.

cuts.speaker: Jenny
cuts.dialogue: Jenny: The little rabbit crossed the...

cuts.speaker: Jenny
cuts.dialogue: Jenny: Briggle.

cuts.action: One child lets out a tiny laugh. Another child laughs because the first one did.

cuts.speaker: Teacher
cuts.dialogue: Teacher: That’s all right. Try again.

cuts.action: Jenny looks at the word again. It feels much bigger now.

cuts.speaker: Jenny
cuts.dialogue: Jenny: Bridge.

orderedEvents.text: Jenny is back at her desk.
The class has moved on, but Jenny has not.
The worksheet lies in front of her. The word BRIDGE seems to stare back.
Jenny slowly folds the paper smaller and smaller.
She slips the folded worksheet into her school bag.
Final Frame: Jenny holding her bag, the folded worksheet hidden inside.

beats.storyBeat: Back at her desk, Jenny is no longer at the front of the room, but the feeling has stayed in front of her. She folds the worksheet smaller and answers a kind check-in with a tiny false assurance, choosing concealment over connection before the school bell releases her with the shame hidden in her bag.
beats.want: Jenny wants the moment to be over and for nobody to look closely at her hurt.
beats.need: She needs permission to admit she is not all right without becoming the mistake.
beats.kidRead: Even after class moves on, your stomach can still feel stuck in the bad moment.
beats.adultRead: The polite ‘I’m fine’ masks the real emotional event: Jenny is beginning to hide rather than process the shame.
beats.emotionalIntent: Keep this quiet and recognisable; the drama is in the mismatch between Jenny’s nod and the truth of her posture.

cuts.speaker: Classmate
cuts.dialogue: Classmate: You all right?

cuts.speaker: Jenny

cuts.action: She slips the folded worksheet into her school bag.

orderedEvents.text: Shot 03: The Feeling Goes Into The Box
Jenny kneels on her bedroom floor.
Her decorated shoebox sits beside her bed. It has stars, hearts and one wonky rainbow drawn on the lid.
Inside are small treasures: a ribbon, a pebble, an old badge, a folded card.
She places the folded worksheet inside the box.
For a moment, she keeps her hand on it.

orderedEvents.speaker: Jenny
orderedEvents.text: I don’t want to think about it.
The box gives the smallest cardboard sigh.
Final Frame: The closed shoebox on the bedroom floor.

beats.storyBeat: In her bedroom, Jenny brings the folded worksheet to her decorated shoebox, a safe place for treasured things. She tries to make the feeling disappear by placing it inside and closing the lid, not noticing that the box has received more than paper: it has received the feeling she cannot carry alone.
beats.want: Jenny wants to put the worksheet away and stop thinking about the classroom mistake.
beats.need: She needs the hidden feeling to be met, not buried.
beats.kidRead: Jenny hides the paper because looking at it hurts.
beats.adultRead: The shoebox becomes a child’s private emotional container: a tender coping strategy that also signals isolation.
beats.emotionalIntent: Make the action intimate and gentle, with the box feeling like a confidant even before the magic answers.

beats.need: The hidden shame needs a safe responder.

beats.adultRead: The fantasy externalises emotional processing: care begins when the child is no longer consciously defending against the feeling.

beats.storyBeat: The Fold receives the call in the middle of Patch and Nib’s wobbly routine, turning comic imbalance into mission focus. treatments.name: Treatment 1 — The Room That Takes a Breath
treatments.audienceExperience: The audience should feel they have entered a classroom that is holding its breath around one enormous mistake. At first BRIGGLE is funny because it is too proud of itself, but the comedy slowly reveals the hurt underneath: the word has become the whole room. The experience moves from nervous giggles, to concern for Jenny’s echo, to relief when the monsters stop trying to defeat the word and start making the room safe enough to breathe.
treatments.emotionalPointOfView: We align with Patch learning to slow down. The room is not staged as a villain arena; it is Jenny’s shame made too large. Patch’s emotional turn is visible in his body: from first-responder momentum toward the giant word, to lowering himself near Jenny’s echo and letting stillness do the work. The audience should understand the lesson before it is stated: staying close is braver than rushing at the problem.
treatments.comicOrDramaticMechanism: Comedy comes from BRIGGLE behaving absurdly important, the furniture seeming embarrassed, and Nib treating a wrong word as a business opportunity. Dramatic pressure comes from the room responding to each attempted fix: certainty makes Jenny’s echo smaller, while gentle play makes BRIGGLE lose its power. The machine is not a gag machine; it is a comic version of the wrong kind of help.
treatments.characterPerformanceStrategy: Patch begins slightly ahead of himself, trying to assess and reassure, then softens into careful nearness. Rumble stays spacious and protective, using his size to make the room feel less like a test. Tilly performs usefulness as precision: quick unfolding, careful diagnosis, then visible recalibration when the machine hurts instead of helps. Nib never mocks Jenny; his odd logic lets the forbidden word become shareable. Jenny’s echo performs the whole emotional journey through small changes: curled inward, hands loosening, a near-smile, laughter, then standing taller.
treatments.visualGrammar: The scene is composed around pressure and release. The giant word, board, machine and folded walls use upright, rigid, accusing shapes. The repair language uses lower poses, curved pathways, shared space and warmer pockets of light. The frame remains wide enough for full-body acting and the room’s emotional mechanics; no cropped characters or key props. The word BRIGGLE should dominate early frames without turning the scene into a monster fight.
treatments.cameraCharacterRelationship: The camera behaves like another careful helper in the room: curious, present, never judging. It discovers the space with the monsters, then lowers and steadies when Patch sits with Jenny’s echo. It should not automatically cut to every speaker; it should stay where the emotional balance is changing. When Tilly’s machine starts, the camera lets the machine invade the group’s space. When Patch names the fear, the camera gives him, Jenny’s echo and Rumble-held walls the same emotional field.
treatments.movementVersusStillness: Arrival has tumbling, echoing, unsettled movement. Patch’s approach to Jenny’s echo slows the scene on purpose. Tilly’s machine reintroduces clunky, repetitive motion and makes the room tighten. Rumble’s holding creates strained stillness against the folding walls. Nib’s café idea releases the tension into light, shared play. The final handle turn should feel rhythmic and modest, not triumphant machinery.
treatments.depthAndEnvironment: Depth is used as emotional scale. Early on, BRIGGLE sits deep and high near the board, making Jenny’s echo feel small in the same wide environment. Desks, chairs and classroom materials subtly lean inward as the shame grows. Rumble’s protective action should visibly create a pocket of usable space. The environment is always made from Jenny’s school materials inside the shoebox shame world, so the classroom feels remembered, not realistic.
treatments.rhythmAndEscalation: Start with echo repetition and visual overwhelm. Let the first jokes land dryly, then tighten as Jenny’s echo is found. The scene dips into quiet for Patch’s non-laughing promise, rises into the machine’s hard correctness, peaks as the walls fold inward, then turns on Patch naming the fear. Nib’s café reframing should not be rushed; the audience needs time to realise they are laughing with the mistake instead of at Jenny. The repair is a gradual warming breath.
treatments.cutPhilosophy: Cuts should follow changes in emotional pressure, not dialogue turns. Hold wider compositions through awkward pauses so the audience can see who is helping and who is accidentally making things worse. Cut when the room changes state: BRIGGLE grows, Jenny’s echo shrinks, the walls press, Patch settles, the game catches, the machine becomes something new. Avoid mechanical action-consequence-reaction coverage.
treatments.openingImage: A wide, slightly low view of the cardboard classroom with BRIGGLE looming near the board, echoing into the room while desks and chairs seem to hunch away from it. The monsters have just arrived low in the space, small against the word’s confidence.
treatments.closingImage: The same classroom now resized and warmed: BRIDGE sits calmly where BRIGGLE dominated, Jenny’s echo stands taller in the shared space, and repair light rises upward from the Try Again Machine and golden card like the room has finally exhaled.
treatments.cinematographerChallenge: Do not make this a standard classroom wide with the characters lined up under the word. The camera must let the room’s pressure be visible in depth, height and negative space. Challenge any staging that parks BRIGGLE as background signage; it must feel like an emotional weight that the frame has to live with, then gradually survive.

treatments.name: Treatment 2 — The Test Room Becomes a Playground
treatments.audienceExperience: The audience first feels trapped in the world of being tested: everything seems to point, measure, correct and repeat. The humour arrives because the test world has overdone itself so badly that it becomes ridiculous. The emotional lift comes when the monsters turn one forbidden wrong word into something playable, proving that a mistake can be handled without making Jenny disappear inside it.
treatments.emotionalPointOfView: This version is told from the group’s shared misdiagnosis, then Patch’s correction of course. They enter treating the room as a problem to solve. Tilly gives that impulse its clearest form with the Correct Answer Machine. Patch’s growth happens when he sees that the room is not asking for the right answer yet; it is asking whether Jenny’s echo can still belong in the room while the mistake is present.
treatments.comicOrDramaticMechanism: The mechanism is a change of rules. In the first half, the room plays by test rules: repeat, correct, shrink, point, press. In the second half, Nib introduces play rules: name it, imagine it, order soup from it, let it be silly. Same word, new social contract. The comedy is dry and character-led because each monster joins differently: Patch supports, Rumble orders simply, Tilly still notices spelling, Nib accepts bad soup as part of the idea.
treatments.characterPerformanceStrategy: Patch starts in practical leader mode, alert and protective, then becomes emotionally honest and lower to the ground. Rumble does not perform panic; he performs careful effort, including the honest adjustment from having it to only having some of it. Tilly should be genuinely pleased with her diagnosis, then genuinely unsettled by the unintended outcome; her change is not humiliation, it is learning. Nib treats the mistake as found treasure, not a punchline. Jenny’s echo should never be played as foolish; she is carrying pressure, then slowly recognising safety.
treatments.visualGrammar: The visual language begins as a test: straight rows, upright board, hard repeated word, a machine that insists on the vertical certainty of correctness. When the café game begins, the room’s geometry becomes less strict: desks can become counters, the huge word can feel like a sign instead of an accusation, the group gathers in an uneven but welcoming arrangement. Keep the handmade cardboard logic visible so the transformation feels tactile and child-clear.
treatments.cameraCharacterRelationship: The camera starts slightly institutional, as if the room is watching the characters be graded. It keeps enough distance to show the accusing layout. As Patch chooses nearness, the camera shifts allegiance from the test to the child’s echo, finding a warmer level without becoming intimate or cropped. During the café play, the camera becomes more permissive, allowing the group’s odd social circle to form in the wide frame.
treatments.movementVersusStillness: The first movement is reactive: arrival tumble, quick looks to the word, Tilly’s purposeful setup. The machine creates repetitive, joyless motion. The walls folding inward create pressured movement from the environment, not the characters. Patch’s truth is anchored in stillness. Nib’s idea creates small improvisational movement: the room’s objects and the monsters’ attention rearrange around a pretend café rather than an exam.
treatments.depthAndEnvironment: Depth shows the shift from being watched to being together. Early depth separates Jenny’s echo near the board from the monsters, with the giant word claiming the vertical background. The machine occupies mid-depth like an official barrier. Rumble’s holding action opens a safe pocket. By the end, depth compresses less threateningly: the group, word, machine and golden card all belong in one repaired classroom instead of competing zones of shame.
treatments.rhythmAndEscalation: The rhythm is rule-bound at first: echo, diagnosis, correction, consequence. The repeated MACHINE line should feel increasingly oppressive because of its sameness. The escalation peaks when the test rules physically reduce Jenny’s echo and the room presses in. Patch interrupts the rule system with personal truth. Nib then breaks the rhythm with sideways logic, and the scene relaxes into a warmer, slightly wonky group game before the repair clicks into place.
treatments.cutPhilosophy: In the test half, cuts can feel more abrupt and rule-driven, but still motivated by pressure changes rather than simple speaker coverage. In the play half, favor longer holds that let the audience see the group deciding not to be embarrassed. Do not cut away from Jenny’s echo’s first smile too quickly; it is the emotional proof that the mechanism has changed.
treatments.openingImage: A wide classroom arrangement that feels like a test has swollen out of control: BRIGGLE high and bossy, board and desks aligned toward Jenny’s echo, the monsters newly landed in the wrong kind of room.
treatments.closingImage: The former test room now reads like a repaired handmade space: the Try Again Machine sits where the Correct Answer Machine was, the golden card catches warm light, and the word has settled back into BRIDGE without needing to be shouted down.
treatments.cinematographerChallenge: Resist safe symmetrical classroom staging. If we make the room too neat, shame feels polite. Let the test geometry feel oppressive at first, then visibly loosen. The biggest visual risk is treating Nib’s café idea as a random gag; frame it as a spatial takeover, where play literally changes how the room is organised.

treatments.name: Treatment 3 — Inside the Echo
treatments.audienceExperience: The audience should feel that BRIGGLE is not just written in the room; it is bouncing around inside everyone’s chest. The scene is funny because the echo is over-serious and oddly musical, but underneath, the repetition becomes exhausting. Relief comes when the repetition changes from shame copying itself into the softer rhythm of trying again.
treatments.emotionalPointOfView: This treatment follows sound made visible. Patch’s journey is to stop answering the noise and start listening to the person underneath it. Jenny’s echo is the quiet centre of a loud room. The audience should feel Patch notice that every loud fix only adds another echo, while every gentle act reduces the need for the room to shout.
treatments.comicOrDramaticMechanism: The dramatic mechanism is repetition versus variation. BRIGGLE repeats without meaning, the machine repeats correctness without comfort, and the folding walls repeat the classroom moment as pressure. Nib’s café idea gives the word new uses, breaking the loop. The comedy comes from unexpected variation: sploon, beautiful-but-wrong, soup, bread, spelling, soup again. The mistake becomes flexible, so it can shrink.
treatments.characterPerformanceStrategy: Patch listens before he leads; even his braver lines should be spoken as something he has felt, not as a lesson he is delivering. Rumble’s performance is about absorbing pressure: steady, kind, honest when the room is too much. Tilly’s precision is audible and physical: she is tuned to diagnosis and correction until she recognises the wrong rhythm. Nib is syncopation: quick, odd, arriving just off the expected beat with the truth. Jenny’s echo moves from closed silence to tiny participation through hands, posture, smile and laugh.
treatments.visualGrammar: Make echo visible through repeating cardboard forms: duplicated word fragments, layered paper edges, desks and wall folds that seem to answer the word back. The giant BRIGGLE is not only a prop; it is the source of ripples in the environment. The repair changes the pattern: repeated hard shapes give way to turning, circling, warming movement around the Try Again Machine handle and the golden card.
treatments.cameraCharacterRelationship: The camera behaves as if it is inside the echo chamber at first, gently unsettled by repeated directions of sound and pressure. It should drift to discover where the echo lands: on the word, on the furniture, on Jenny’s echo, on the monsters’ attempts to help. When Patch kneels, the camera steadies because he has found the true centre. In the final repair, the camera rides the calmer rhythm of the handle and rising light without turning it into spectacle.
treatments.movementVersusStillness: Movement begins as vibration: tumble, word echo, furniture embarrassment, tiny environmental flinches. Patch’s approach reduces movement. The Correct Answer Machine makes movement mechanical and repetitive, and the walls add a slow inward fold. Rumble’s resistance is held effort. Patch’s truth creates a pause where the room can hear something other than BRIGGLE. Nib’s play introduces light, irregular movement, then Tilly’s transformed machine turns that irregularity into a steady try-again rhythm.
treatments.depthAndEnvironment: Use layered depth like an echo: foreground cardboard edges, mid-ground monsters, background board and word, with repeated shapes creating a sense that one mistake has multiplied. Jenny’s echo should be visible but not isolated by a cruel spotlight; the room’s pressure should explain her inwardness. As the repair works, the layers stop crowding and become readable pathways for warm light to travel upward toward the real world.
treatments.rhythmAndEscalation: The rhythm starts with the BRIGGLE echo setting the pulse. Dialogue sits against that pulse: Patch’s first dry observation, Rumble’s plain naming, Tilly’s diagnosis, Nib’s furniture truth. The machine then locks the rhythm into hard certainty. The walls pressing inward create the loudest emotional passage. Patch’s two truth lines should be the quietest turn in the scene. Nib’s café exchange loosens the beat into comic give-and-take, and the final handle turn becomes the new pulse.
treatments.cutPhilosophy: Cuts should be musical but not flashy: follow the echo’s pressure, then the interruption of that pressure. Hold when silence matters. Let repeated lines create expectation, then cut only when a new kind of response appears. The final sequence should not cut like a victory montage; it should feel like one continuous repair rhythm carrying the room from BRIGGLE back to BRIDGE.
treatments.openingImage: A wide view through layered cardboard classroom edges, as if the audience is inside the echo itself: BRIGGLE’s repeated presence seems to bounce from board to walls to furniture while the monsters tumble into the vibration of the mistake.
treatments.closingImage: A wide, calm classroom where the echo has become a gentle upward rhythm: Patch at the Try Again Machine handle, Jenny’s echo taller nearby, BRIDGE restored, and warm repair light lifting out through the shoebox world.
treatments.cinematographerChallenge: Do not literalise the echo with busy visual clutter that steals acting space. The challenge is to make repetition felt while preserving clean, wide performance readability. Avoid default speaker cutting; the camera must track how sound pressure changes the room and how stillness finally interrupts it.

treatmentSelection.selectedTreatment: Treatment 1 — The Room That Takes a Breath, strengthened with Treatment 3’s echo-as-pressure rhythm
combinedFrom: Treatment 1 — The Room That Takes a Breath
treatmentSelection.governingAudienceExperience: The audience feels a classroom holding its breath around one enormous mistake, then feels the breath return when the mistake becomes safe to stay near, play with, and try again.
treatmentSelection.rationale: Treatment 1 is the strongest spine because it protects the emotional truth: this is not a battle with a bad word, it is Jenny’s shame making the room too small to breathe in. It gives Patch a specific, visible change from rushing at the problem to lowering himself beside Jenny’s echo, and it keeps the humour kind: BRIGGLE is absurdly proud, Nib reframes it without mocking Jenny, and the room itself shows the cost of wrong help. Treatment 3 adds the best sensory engine: shame copying itself as echo, then changing into the calmer rhythm of trying again. That gives the scene a memorable sound-and-space identity without needing extra explanation. Treatment 2 has a useful clarity around test rules becoming play rules, but as a full governing treatment it is more schematic and risks making the scene feel like a concept demonstration. We should retain only its strongest practical insight: Nib’s café play must be staged as a spatial takeover, not a random gag. The selected approach gives us contrast, rhythm and feasibility: one wide handmade classroom plate can transform through pressure, depth, furniture lean, repeated word fragments, machine rhythm, Rumble’s held space, and a gradual warm release. It also honours the audience journey: funny first, then worried, then quietly relieved.
treatmentSelection.rejectionChecks: No selected element depends on fixed character lanes; characters may shift position according to pressure, protection, invention and play. No selected element requires keeping all characters visible at all times; the wide frame preserves full-body readability, but attention follows the emotional pressure. No habitual action/reaction coverage is accepted; cuts are motivated by state changes in the room and Jenny’s echo, not by speaker turns. No safe classroom setup is accepted; BRIGGLE must occupy depth, height and negative space as an emotional weight, not background signage. No repeated close-up punctuation is accepted; the scene remains wide and performance-led. No mechanical shot-count thinking is accepted at this stage. Generic terms are not enough; the direction must be observable: folding walls, leaning desks, hard machine rhythm, Patch lowering, Rumble holding space, Nib rearranging shame into play, warm repair light rising. Treatment 2 is not selected as the main treatment because its test-to-play structure risks becoming too rule-bound and illustrative; it is only mined for the spatial-play insight. Treatment 3 is accepted only as a disciplined overlay; if the echo visuals become busy clutter that steals acting space, they must be reduced.

scene.purpose: Inside Jenny’s shoebox shame classroom, the monsters discover that one wrong word has become the whole room, then change the repair from correctness to safe nearness, shared play and trying again.
scene.dramaticQuestion: Can Patch help Jenny’s emotional echo feel big enough to meet the mistake again without making the shame louder?
scene.connectionFromPreviousScene: The Fold’s call has brought the monsters into Jenny’s hidden emotional world after she hides the worksheet in her shoebox.
scene.handoverToNextScene: The room has exhaled: BRIGGLE can become BRIDGE, Jenny’s echo stands taller, and the repair light rises toward Jenny’s real morning.

beats.sourceScript: The monsters tumble into a cardboard classroom built from Jenny’s school materials, where BRIGGLE has become huge, echoing and absurdly self-important. They recognise that the feeling has built a whole room around one moment, then see Jenny’s emotional echo, small and curled inward near the board.

beats.sourceScript: Tilly, trying to be useful, unfolds a machine designed to produce correctness. The device clunks out certainty, but Jenny’s echo shrinks and BRIGGLE grows. Rumble sees the harm, Tilly stops, and Patch realises that being correct is not the same as helping someone feel better.

Patch: That sounds... very answer-y.
MACHINE: Correct. Correct. Correct. Correct.
Rumble: She is getting smaller.
Tilly: That was not the intended outcome.
Patch: Maybe correct is not the same as better.

beats.sourceScript: The shame world tightens as the walls fold inward and the repeated word gets louder. Then he separates the mistake from Jenny’s size, and the room pauses long enough for Tilly to understand what has to change.

The others join the game with gentle sincerity, and Jenny’s echo smiles, then laughs. BRIGGLE shrinks because it is no longer only evidence against her; it has become something she can play with.

shots.physicalPerformance: Tilly moves with brisk purpose, opening her tool roll and unfolding the device into the safe space. Patch’s body holds a small hesitation before the handle turns. As Tilly cranks, cards scatter across the floor, Jenny’s echo visibly reduces, and the wall word gains size. Tilly’s smile nearly escapes, Nib gives a small shrug, Jenny’s echo laughs softly, and the wall word shrinks behind them.

direction.premise: A classroom reading mistake follows Jenny home until her shoebox calls the Box Monsters into a handmade shame world built around one too-large wrong word.
direction.dramaticQuestion: Can the monsters help Jenny carry the mistake differently before shame makes her feel too small to try again?
direction.theme: Getting something wrong does not make you small.
direction.externalJourney: Jenny misreads a word, hides the worksheet in her shoebox, and the monsters travel from The Fold into a cardboard classroom where the mistaken word has swollen into the room’s bossy centrepiece. Their attempted fix fails, then they transform the machine and the meaning of the mistake so Jenny can face the word again.
direction.internalJourney: Jenny moves from public embarrassment, to hiding, to a tiny private openness, to reclaiming the mistake with humour, and finally to trying again while still feeling nervous.
direction.relationshipChanges: Patch begins as a brave responder who wants to help quickly, but earns Jenny’s echo’s trust by sitting with her instead of fixing her. Tilly shifts from controlling the outcome to redesigning her solution around emotional truth. Rumble protects space rather than forcing confidence. Nib’s odd humour becomes the safe bridge between shame and self-acceptance.
direction.emotionalCurve: Quiet pressure builds into embarrassment, then withdrawal, then magical concern. The middle tightens as the wrong fix makes shame heavier. Relief arrives first through being met gently, then through laughter that belongs to Jenny rather than at Jenny. The ending lands in soft courage and secret warmth.
direction.comedyCurve: The comedy starts as character imbalance in The Fold, turns into dry diagnosis and wonky tools, dips during the failed fix, then returns as Nib’s sideways cafe idea makes the mistake feel usable rather than poisonous. The final joke is small, affectionate and earned.
direction.setupPayoffMap: The word BRIDGE becomes BRIGGLE in class, then grows into the shame world’s looming word, then shrinks through laughter, becomes BRIDGE again, and returns in the classroom as a word Jenny can say. Jenny folds the worksheet smaller when ashamed, then later carries it without folding it. The Correct Answer Machine fails, then becomes the Try Again Machine. The shoebox’s first sigh and call pay off as its warm twitch and The Fold lamp glow.
direction.visualMotifs: Folding paper as shrinking self-worth; oversized lettering as shame taking up too much space; golden tape and cards as repair, not erasure; cardboard walls pressing inward and later opening with warmth; the shoebox as a private container that becomes a gentle doorway.
direction.sonicMotifs: Classroom quiet, tiny laugh, bell, cardboard sigh, pulse through floorboards, Fold honk, echoing repeated mistake, clunking machine, soft laugh, warm final glow.
direction.climax: Patch names the emotional truth that being wrong did not make Jenny small, allowing Tilly to change the machine’s purpose and Jenny’s echo to receive the golden repair card.
direction.resolution: Jenny wakes to the repaired worksheet and card, returns to class, reads the line correctly, gently jokes about the earlier mistake, and smiles as the secret magic remains unseen.
direction.intendedFinalFeeling: A warm, private courage: the feeling is still remembered, but it is no longer bigger than Jenny.

storyTruth.protagonist: Jenny, carried emotionally by Patch as the monster who most actively meets her shame.
storyTruth.falseBelief: If everyone sees a mistake, the mistake makes you smaller.
storyTruth.practicalWant: Jenny wants to hide the worksheet and stop thinking about the misread word.
storyTruth.keyRelationship: Jenny’s emotional echo and Patch, with the ensemble learning how to support rather than correct her.
storyTruth.emotionalFearOrWound: Public laughter turns one reading mistake into the fear that she is ridiculous and exposed.
storyTruth.transformedAction: Jenny keeps the repaired worksheet open, returns to class, reads the line, and lets herself make a gentle joke about the mistake.
storyTruth.themeProvenThroughAction: The episode proves that wrong is not the same as small by having Jenny try again without hiding the evidence of having been wrong.

northStar.theme: Getting something wrong does not make you small.
northStar.childClearWant: Jenny wants the loud wrong word to stop pointing at her.

scenePurposeAndEmotionalChange.purpose: Inside Jenny’s shoebox shame classroom, the monsters discover that one wrong word has become the whole room, then change the repair from correctness to safe nearness, shared play and trying again.
scenePurposeAndEmotionalChange.dramaticQuestion: Can Patch help Jenny’s emotional echo feel big enough to meet the mistake again without making the shame louder?
scenePurposeAndEmotionalChange.entry: If a feeling is frightening, a brave helper should get in fast and make the scary thing stop.
scenePurposeAndEmotionalChange.exit: He turns the transformed Try Again Machine handle as the room warms and BRIGGLE can become BRIDGE.

dramaticBeats.beginning: The room shifts from unknown shoebox space into a clear shame classroom dominated by one loud wrong word, and the monsters locate Jenny’s emotional echo inside that pressure.
dramaticBeats.development: The room pauses; Tilly can see what the machine must become, and Jenny’s echo is no longer alone inside the fear.
dramaticBeats.turn: Tilly transforms the Correct Answer Machine into a Try Again Machine, and Patch turns the handle with a rhythmic, modest motion.
dramaticBeats.landing: The scene hands over to morning with relief rather than triumph: the feeling is carryable now.

performanceDirection.principalPerformance: Patch begins ahead of himself, recovers from the tumble, jokes lightly, then visibly redirects his attention from the loud word to Jenny’s echo.
performanceDirection.physicalPerformance: The group lands low and untidy, then each body recovers into a different read of the room: Patch pops up first and tracks upward, Rumble shields one ear, Tilly scans the classroom like a diagram, and Nib tests a desk with one curious poke. By the end, all their attention drops from the oversized wall word to Jenny’s curled echo near the board.

contract.playableIntention: Patch enters ready to deal with the biggest visible problem, then notices the hurt person inside the room instead.

phases.observableAction: The oversized wall word dominates the board area, its echo rattles the paper surfaces, and the desks and chairs hunch inward.
Patch recovers from the tumble fastest, plants himself low, and looks up at the looming lettering.
Tilly steadies herself, scans the board, walls and desks in order, and fixes her attention on the classroom pattern rather than the noise alone.
Patch’s gaze leaves the high lettering and travels lower through the room until it lands on Jenny’s emotional echo near the board.

contract.physicalCauseAndEffect: The tumble throws the monsters into low positions; the echo makes the room flinch and draws their eyes upward; the group’s shared sightline then redirects through the desks to the curled echo.
contract.visibleEmotionalTurn: Bodies move from scrambled arrival and dry room-reading into a quieter, lower focus on Jenny’s emotional echo.
contract.requiredLanding: The final image reads as the monsters having found Jenny’s emotional echo inside the classroom pressure, with the oversized word still looming above and behind her.
contract.performanceFreedom: Animators may vary the exact recovery order, blinks, wobble settles, desk squeak reaction and small furniture shivers, while preserving the upward-to-lower eyeline turn and the final concern hold.

characterTruths.canonTrait: Brave, warm first responder who learns by staying with the feeling.
characterTruths.playableWant: Find what needs help before the room gets worse.
characterTruths.pressureResponse: He starts by orienting toward the biggest, loudest object, then reins in his charge when he sees Jenny’s echo.
characterTruths.observableSignature: Quickest recovery from the tumble, forward lean, fast upward look, then a visible softening and lower eyeline.
characterTruths.substitutionTest: Rumble would protect the space, Tilly would analyse the system, and Nib would poke at the oddness; only Patch makes the shift from responder momentum to person-facing attention the shot’s main turn.

characterTruths.substitutionTest: Patch would move toward need, Rumble toward safety, and Nib toward odd evidence; only Tilly makes the room feel like a pattern being diagnosed.

performanceDirection.principalPerformance: Patch moves slowly, sits before asking anything of Jenny’s echo, and makes his own wrong word available for a gentle laugh.
performanceDirection.physicalPerformance: Patch slows his approach before reaching Jenny’s echo, lowers himself to the floor at a respectful distance, and keeps his hands and posture open. Nib’s hand pops up with matter-of-fact precision, Patch accepts being the safe comic target, Rumble lowers his weight carefully into the pocket, and Jenny’s echo moves from downcast avoidance to a tiny look and loosened grip on the worksheet.

contract.playableIntention: Patch chooses not to close the distance all the way; he makes himself safe first and lets Jenny’s echo decide whether to look up.

Patch slows, stops short of her personal space, lowers himself to the floor, and keeps his body open rather than reaching for her.
Nib raises one hand crisply from within the shared frame, adding a small factual beat while staying aimed at Patch, not Jenny’s echo.
Jenny’s emotional echo lifts her attention toward Patch and her hands ease their grip on the worksheet.

contract.physicalCauseAndEffect: Patch’s slowed approach and seated posture reduce pressure; Nib’s small interjection turns Patch into the harmless target; Rumble’s careful sit expands the safe floor space; Jenny’s grip loosens in response.
contract.visibleEmotionalTurn: Jenny’s echo changes from curled avoidance with clenched hands to looking at Patch with the worksheet held less tightly.
contract.requiredLanding: The shot must end with a clear pocket of safety: Patch seated apart from Jenny’s echo, Rumble settled carefully nearby, and Jenny’s hands visibly loosened.
contract.performanceFreedom: Allow natural variation in how Patch folds down, how Nib’s hand rises, how Rumble manages his weight, and the exact size of Jenny’s almost-look, as long as no one crowds or touches her.

characterTruths.canonTrait: Brave, warm first responder who learns by staying with the feeling.
characterTruths.playableWant: Become trustworthy enough for Jenny’s echo to stay present with him.
characterTruths.pressureResponse: He suppresses his usual forward rush and lowers himself instead of taking over the space.

performanceDirection.principalPerformance: Tilly performs usefulness as speed and precision, then stops herself when the visible result contradicts the plan.
performanceDirection.physicalPerformance: Tilly moves with brisk purpose, opening her tool roll and unfolding the device into the safe space. Patch’s body holds a small hesitation before the handle turns. As Tilly cranks, cards scatter across the floor, Jenny’s echo visibly reduces, and the wall word gains size. Rumble clocks the harm first; Tilly arrests the handle mid-process, and Patch looks from the stopped device to the reduced echo with chastened understanding.

contract.playableIntention: Tilly genuinely tries to help by applying a precise fix, then has to stop when the visible result proves the tool is hurting the space.

phases.observableAction: Tilly opens her tool roll, unfolds the cardboard device with tidy speed, and positions it inside the group’s shared floor space.
Tilly turns the handle in a steady working rhythm as the device clunks and throws cards outward across the floor.
Jenny’s emotional echo pulls inward and becomes visibly reduced while the wall lettering grows larger behind her.
Tilly stops the handle, holds her hands still on the machine, and looks at the reduced echo and scattered cards.

contract.physicalCauseAndEffect: Tilly’s handle turn activates the device; the clunking output sends cards into the safe area; that hard certainty causes Jenny’s echo to reduce and the wall word to enlarge; Rumble’s noticing leads Tilly to stop the motion.
contract.visibleEmotionalTurn: Tilly changes from efficient confidence to still recalibration, while Jenny’s echo changes from newly safer to visibly diminished again.
contract.requiredLanding: The final frame must read that the machine has made things worse: stopped handle, scattered cards, darker classroom, enlarged wall word and Jenny’s echo reduced beyond the device.
contract.performanceFreedom: Allow invention details, card trajectories, crank resistance and Tilly’s exact flustered stillness to vary, but keep the cause-and-effect between handle, cards, echo reduction and machine stop unmistakable.

characterTruths.canonTrait: Organiser and inventor who loves systems and tools, and learns that feelings need listening before fixing.
characterTruths.playableWant: Produce a useful answer quickly enough to relieve the classroom pressure.

performanceDirection.principalPerformance: Patch kneels close without crowding, names his own fear plainly, and holds still long enough for Jenny’s echo and the room to hear it.
performanceDirection.physicalPerformance: The room tightens around the group as the walls fold inward. Rumble plants both hands against one wall and pushes with careful strength, but his feet slide under the pressure. Patch uses the space Rumble holds to kneel near Jenny’s echo, keeps from touching her, places a hand on his own chest, and stays steady as she looks at him. The walls stop, the wall word flickers, and Tilly’s attention shifts to the machine with a new idea.

contract.playableIntention: Patch uses the temporary space Rumble creates to stay beside Jenny’s echo and name the fear without turning it into another fix.

phases.observableAction: The cardboard walls fold inward, the room narrows, and the high wall lettering flickers and grows more insistent.
Rumble braces both hands against one wall, pushes back, and slides on the floor while keeping part of the space open.
Patch kneels near Jenny’s emotional echo, keeps his body low, and places one hand on his own chest while looking at her.
The walls stop moving, the wall word flickers instead of pressing the room, and the classroom holds still.

contract.physicalCauseAndEffect: The folding walls reduce usable space; Rumble’s bracing slows one side enough for Patch to kneel near Jenny’s echo; Patch’s low, self-directed gesture draws her eye contact; the room’s movement halts and Tilly can re-read the machine.

contract.requiredLanding: End with the room halted: Rumble still braced, Patch low beside Jenny’s echo without touching her, Tilly turned toward the machine, and the wall pressure paused.
contract.performanceFreedom: Animators may vary cardboard creases, Rumble’s foot slide distance, Patch’s kneel shape and Tilly’s realisation beat, provided the protected space and final halt remain clear.

performanceDirection.physicalPerformance: Nib darts into the paused space, gathers cardboard and pencil, writes a cafe sign using the charged word, and holds it up with earnest pride. Tilly stares in baffled precision. Nib waits through the tiny silence without pushing, Jenny’s echo lets a first smile appear, and the others join the pretend game with gentle sincerity. Tilly’s smile nearly escapes, Nib gives a small shrug, Jenny’s echo laughs softly, and the wall word shrinks behind them.

phases.observableAction: Nib finds a scrap and pencil, writes a small sign, and raises it proudly in the shared floor space.

elevenLabsV3VoiceAndTiming.listenerRule: Only the active speaker articulates; listeners remain silent and closed-mouth.

performances.speaker: BRIGGLE ECHO
performances.voiceIdentity: Jenny’s shame echo: small, repetitive, stuck on the word rather than performing it; sound comes from the room as much as from a speaker.
performances.dramaticIntention: Keep the mistake present and unavoidable.
performances.subtext: This is the only thing the feeling can say right now.
performances.relationshipTarget: The whole group and the classroom space.
performances.emotionalExit: Still looping, but about to be noticed as hurt rather than noise.
performances.pace: Slow, heavy repetition with no comic bounce.
performances.rhythm: Same word three times, each slightly flatter and more trapped.
performances.pauses: A small dead-air gap after each full stop; do not rush into the next repetition.
performances.breaths: Almost breathless, as if the echo is being pushed out by the wall word.
performances.nonVerbalActions: The oversized word dominates the room while the group lands untidily below it.
performances.elevenLabsV3Direction: ElevenLabs text: [distant, small, echoing] Briggle. [short hollow pause] Briggle. [short hollow pause] Briggle.
performances.physicalActionRelationship: Play against the group’s tumble: the echo is not reacting to them, it is already trapped in the shame loop.
performances.expectedTiming: Begin under the loose landing momentum; let the final repetition hang as Patch pops up and tracks upward.

performances.breaths: Small recovery breath before the line.
performances.nonVerbalActions: Patch pops up first and looks upward at the oversized wall word.
performances.elevenLabsV3Direction: ElevenLabs text: [quick recovery breath, lightly amused] That word has got very confident.

performances.subtext: I accept the play, but I still notice the letters.
performances.relationshipTarget: Nib, Jenny’s echo, and the team.
performances.emotionalExit: A smile almost escapes.
performances.rhythm: Small technical note placed inside the pretend game.
performances.pauses: Tiny pause before “would,” as if choosing not to overcorrect.
performances.breaths: Small restrained smile-breath before the line.
performances.nonVerbalActions: Tilly’s smile nearly escapes as she joins with gentle sincerity.
performances.elevenLabsV3Direction: ElevenLabs text: [dry, precise, softening] The spelling would need work.

performances.subtext: Yes, and that is allowed too.
performances.relationshipTarget: Tilly and Jenny’s echo.
performances.emotionalExit: Light, open, ready for Jenny’s laugh.

performances.pauses: Tiny beat after Tilly before answering.
performances.breaths: Little shrug-breath before speaking.
performances.nonVerbalActions: Nib gives a small shrug.
performances.elevenLabsV3Direction: ElevenLabs text: [tiny shrug, matter-of-fact] So would the soup.

performances.emotionalExit: Soft relief as the word shrinks.

performances.breaths: Soft relieved breath before speaking.
performances.nonVerbalActions: Jenny’s echo laughs softly; the wall word shrinks behind them.
