stagePlan.purpose: Land the audience inside a remembered classroom organised around one oversized wrong word.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: The monsters tumble into the cardboard classroom and the huge wall word echoes through the space, making the desks and chairs seem to hunch away.
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: Arrival chaos turns into nervous giggle-pressure: the mistake is absurdly proud of itself before it becomes painful.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Begin wide and slightly low, letting the room depth run up toward the board; the camera settles after the tumble instead of chasing every body.
stagePlan.observableEndState: All four monsters are low in the room under the looming wall word as the echo continues.

stagePlan.purpose: Let the team read the room without turning the word into a monster fight.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: Patch looks up, Rumble covers one ear, Tilly studies the classroom, and Nib pokes a squeaking desk while the lines play in order: “That word has got very confident.” “It is a loud mistake.” “This is the moment. The feeling has built itself around it.” “Even the furniture is embarrassed.”
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: Dry observations keep the fear playable while Tilly’s diagnosis shifts the room from joke to feeling-place.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Hold a broad shared frame with tiny adjustments of height and drift so the word, furniture and group all remain in one pressured field.
stagePlan.observableEndState: The embarrassed furniture lean, the squeaked desk settles, and the group’s attention begins to move past the word.

stagePlan.purpose: Reveal who the giant mistake is hurting.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: The monsters look ahead and find Jenny’s emotional echo small and curled inward near the board.
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: The nervous laugh catches in the audience’s throat; the mistake becomes an emotional weight, not just a funny object.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: The camera lets the sightline travel through the room depth to the board instead of cutting to a standard reveal.
stagePlan.observableEndState: The monsters have visibly found Jenny’s emotional echo inside the pressure.

coverage.purpose: Discover the shame classroom as the monsters do.
coverage.framingAndCamera: Wide, slightly low in-world view from classroom floor height, with the giant wall word high and deep near the board and the monsters arriving low in the foreground space.
coverage.storyAction: The monsters tumble in as the echo says, “Briggle. Briggle. Briggle.”
coverage.performanceFocus: Tumbling bodies recover into looking-up stillness; Patch’s first-responder energy starts faster than the room will allow.
coverage.landingImage: The group is small against the high, overconfident word while furniture leans inward.
coverage.cutReason: This is the opening view; no prior cut.

coverage.purpose: Hold the comic diagnosis in one shared pressure field.
coverage.framingAndCamera: Still wide, with a gentle lateral drift that keeps the word, the group and a squeaking desk visible without isolating speakers.
coverage.storyAction: Patch, Rumble, Tilly and Nib each register the room in character, ending with Nib’s desk poke and line.
coverage.performanceFocus: Patch jokes upward, Rumble protects his ear, Tilly measures the room, Nib treats the furniture as a witness.
coverage.landingImage: Nib’s poked desk has squeaked and settled while Tilly’s attention remains analytical.
coverage.cutReason: The view changes from arrival impact to room-reading; staying on the exact arrival angle would make the dialogue feel parked under signage.

coverage.purpose: Shift the audience from laughing at the oversized word to concern for Jenny’s echo.
coverage.framingAndCamera: A wide sightline through desks toward the board, allowing negative space between the monsters and Jenny’s emotional echo.
coverage.storyAction: The monsters all look ahead and see Jenny’s emotional echo small and curled inward.
coverage.performanceFocus: Patch’s attention softens and drops away from the giant word toward the child-shaped hurt.
coverage.landingImage: The monsters face Jenny’s emotional echo across the cardboard classroom.
coverage.cutReason: The reveal needs a changed information axis; remaining on the group would hide the emotional target too long.

units.closingImage: The monsters stand and crouch in a shared line of attention toward Jenny’s emotional echo near the board.

stagePlan.purpose: Let Patch choose nearness without pressure.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: Jenny’s emotional echo holds the worksheet while Patch approaches slowly and says, “Hello. We are not here to laugh.”
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: The room drops from discovery into careful quiet; Patch’s bravery becomes slowness.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Begin from the prior sightline and lower the camera slightly with Patch, keeping distance visible between him and Jenny’s echo.
stagePlan.observableEndState: Jenny’s echo looks down while Patch remains close but not crowding her.

stagePlan.purpose: Make a wrong word shareable without aiming the laugh at Jenny.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: Patch sits a little distance away and admits, “I have said spoon wrong three times today.” Nib raises a hand: “He said sploon.” Patch accepts it: “Beautiful word. Wrong, but beautiful.”
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: A small laugh becomes safe because Patch offers his own mistake first.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Hold the low shared frame rather than cutting to Nib; the joke belongs to the circle, not to a punch-in.
stagePlan.observableEndState: Jenny’s echo almost looks up.

stagePlan.purpose: Give Jenny permission not to perform instant courage.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: Rumble sits carefully and says, “You do not have to be big yet.” Jenny’s hands loosen slightly.
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: The sploon joke hands into tenderness, creating the first pocket of trust.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Let Rumble’s careful lowering widen the safe pocket inside the same frame; hold on the hands loosening.
stagePlan.observableEndState: Jenny’s echo is looking at Patch with her hands less clenched around the worksheet.

coverage.purpose: Show Patch’s approach as a changed kind of courage.
coverage.framingAndCamera: Wide-low classroom view from near Jenny’s echo’s level, with Patch crossing only part of the distance and leaving air between them.
coverage.storyAction: Patch approaches slowly and promises they are not there to laugh.
coverage.performanceFocus: Patch controls his urgency; Jenny’s echo looks down rather than accepting him immediately.
coverage.landingImage: Patch has stopped at a respectful distance while Jenny’s echo looks down with the worksheet held close.
coverage.cutReason: This is the opening view after the prior reveal; a new low angle is needed because the story has moved from room scale to trust distance.

coverage.purpose: Keep the self-deprecating joke safe by holding the whole small circle.
coverage.framingAndCamera: Wide enough for Patch seated, Jenny’s echo, Nib’s raised hand and Rumble waiting to enter the safe space; no cropped hands or worksheet.
coverage.storyAction: Patch shares his own spoon mistake; Nib supplies the sploon detail; Patch accepts the wrong word warmly.
coverage.performanceFocus: Patch lets himself be the comic target, Nib is exact and odd, Jenny’s echo nearly looks up.
coverage.landingImage: Jenny’s echo’s head has lifted a fraction toward Patch after the shared mistake.
coverage.cutReason: The view shifts only enough to include Nib’s contribution; isolating Nib would make the joke feel like a jab.

coverage.purpose: Land Rumble’s permission and Jenny’s first visible trust.
coverage.framingAndCamera: A gentle widening as Rumble sits carefully, keeping his body part of the protective space rather than a looming shape.
coverage.storyAction: Rumble sits and says Jenny does not have to be big yet; Jenny’s hands loosen.
coverage.performanceFocus: Rumble’s care is in controlled weight; Jenny’s trust is tiny and physical.
coverage.landingImage: Jenny’s echo looks at Patch with loosened hands around the worksheet.
coverage.cutReason: The view changes to include Rumble’s careful sit because it alters the size and safety of the space.

units.closingImage: Jenny’s emotional echo faces Patch across a small pocket of floor space, the worksheet held less tightly.

stagePlan.purpose: Introduce Tilly’s helpfulness as precision that may be the wrong tool.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: Tilly opens her tool roll and unfolds the cardboard device with its Correct Answer Machine sign while saying, “Good news. I have identified the issue.” Patch looks uncertain and says, “That sounds... very answer-y.”
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: The safe pocket is interrupted by organised confidence that is funny because it is too sure of itself.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Cut to the same room with Tilly’s machine entering the group space from the side, letting the object invade rather than staging a clean demonstration.
stagePlan.observableEndState: The machine is fully unfolded in the room, pointed into the emotional space.

stagePlan.purpose: Show certainty producing harm.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: Tilly turns the handle; the machine clunks, spits cards everywhere and says, “Correct. Correct. Correct. Correct.” Jenny’s echo shrinks and the wall word grows larger.
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: Clunky invention comedy flips into worry as the audience sees correctness increase shame.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Let the machine’s movement dominate the foreground while Jenny’s echo and the growing word remain visible in depth.
stagePlan.observableEndState: Cards litter the floor, Jenny’s echo is smaller, and the wall word has gained scale.

stagePlan.purpose: Let the team recognise that the fix is wrong.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: Rumble notices and says, “She is getting smaller.” Tilly stops turning and says, “That was not the intended outcome.” Patch looks at the machine and says, “Maybe correct is not the same as better.”
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: Tilly’s confidence becomes recalibration; Patch learns the rule the audience has just seen.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Hold the stopped machine in the same frame as Jenny’s reduced echo so the line is grounded in visible consequence.
stagePlan.observableEndState: Jenny’s echo is smaller beside the stopped machine, and the classroom has darkened.

coverage.purpose: Make the machine feel like a new pressure entering the safe space.
coverage.framingAndCamera: Wide shared frame from the safe pocket’s side, with Tilly unfolding the device into the middle distance rather than presenting it front-on.
coverage.storyAction: Tilly opens the tool roll, produces the machine, and Patch voices uncertainty.
coverage.performanceFocus: Tilly is quick and precise; Patch’s doubt is small but visible before the handle turns.
coverage.landingImage: The Correct Answer Machine stands assembled inside the group’s space.
coverage.cutReason: This is the opening after a planned boundary; the view must announce a new intervention rather than continue the intimate seated angle.

coverage.purpose: Let the wrong fix physically overrun the room.
coverage.framingAndCamera: Wide with the machine large in the near layer, cards spitting across the floor toward Jenny’s echo and the board visible behind.
coverage.storyAction: The machine clunks out repeated correctness; Jenny’s echo shrinks as the wall word grows.
coverage.performanceFocus: Tilly’s functional rhythm contrasts with Jenny’s visible shrinking; Rumble’s attention starts to shift toward harm.
coverage.landingImage: Cards are scattered, Jenny’s echo is reduced, and the word is larger behind her.
coverage.cutReason: The view changes because the machine’s action becomes the dominant force; staying on setup would hide the cause-and-effect.

coverage.purpose: Hold the cost of correctness long enough for Tilly and Patch to understand it.
coverage.framingAndCamera: Wide, slightly stiller frame with the stopped handle, Tilly, Patch, Rumble, Jenny’s smaller echo and darker room all legible.
coverage.storyAction: Rumble names the shrinking, Tilly stops, and Patch recognises that correctness is not the same as repair.
coverage.performanceFocus: Rumble’s protective noticing, Tilly’s arrested motion, Patch’s chastened look at the machine.
coverage.landingImage: Jenny’s echo is smaller in a darker classroom with the stopped machine between help and harm.
coverage.cutReason: The view changes from mechanical action to moral consequence; a reaction-only cut would weaken the shared accountability.

units.closingImage: Jenny’s smaller echo stands near the board in a darker room while the stopped machine and scattered cards occupy the floor between the helpers and her.

stagePlan.purpose: Escalate the shame from a bad tool to the whole classroom pressing inward.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: The cardboard walls fold inward and the huge wall word repeats louder: “Briggle. Briggle. Briggle.”
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: The room itself becomes the pressure, making the earlier harm feel real rather than theoretical.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Open on the darker room from the prior landing and let the side walls visibly creep inward within a wide frame.
stagePlan.observableEndState: The classroom has narrowed and the repeated word fills the air.

stagePlan.purpose: Give Rumble a protective action that creates temporary space but cannot solve the shame alone.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: Rumble presses both hands against one wall and says, “I have got this.” The wall pushes harder, his feet slide, and he revises, “I have got some of this.”
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: A small truthful laugh under pressure shows protection matters, but strength cannot carry the whole repair.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Hold wide enough to see Rumble’s sliding feet and the threatened safe pocket at once; do not cut for a gag reaction.
stagePlan.observableEndState: Rumble is braced and sliding, holding only part of the room open.

stagePlan.purpose: Let Patch name the fear and separate the mistake from Jenny’s size.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: Patch kneels near Jenny’s echo, says, “When I get something wrong, I feel like everyone can see it.” Jenny’s echo looks at him; Patch places a hand on his chest and says, “But getting it wrong did not make you small.” The room pauses, the wall word flickers, and Tilly looks at her machine with understanding.
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: Physical crisis turns into quiet truth; the audience feels the first real exhale begin.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Lower and steady the frame around Patch, Jenny’s echo and Rumble-held wall so the truth lands inside the same endangered space.
stagePlan.observableEndState: The walls have stopped pressing in.

coverage.purpose: Show the whole room taking over the pressure.
coverage.framingAndCamera: Wide room view with darker cardboard walls bending inward from both sides and the group squeezed around the stopped machine.
coverage.storyAction: The walls begin to fold as the echo repeats louder.
coverage.performanceFocus: Everyone reacts to the environment, not to a single villain; Patch clocks Jenny’s echo first.
coverage.landingImage: The room is visibly narrower around the group.
coverage.cutReason: This is the opening after the machine beat; the new view shows the pressure has become architectural.

coverage.purpose: Make Rumble’s protective effort comic and real in the same image.
coverage.framingAndCamera: Wide side-weighted frame with Rumble bracing a wall and the floor space between Patch and Jenny’s echo still visible.
coverage.storyAction: Rumble claims he has it, then slides and admits he has some of it.
coverage.performanceFocus: Rumble’s careful strength and honest revision; Patch uses the held space rather than watching the gag.
coverage.landingImage: Rumble’s feet have slid while one section of wall remains held back.
coverage.cutReason: The view changes to make the wall pressure and sliding feet readable; staying on the whole-room view would lose Rumble’s character-specific effort.

coverage.purpose: Land Patch’s truth without isolating it from the room and Rumble’s protection.
coverage.framingAndCamera: Low wide-near frame keeping Patch kneeling by Jenny’s echo in the lower field, Rumble’s braced wall at the edge, and the flickering wall word above/deep.
coverage.storyAction: Patch names how a mistake feels visible, then says it did not make Jenny small; the room pauses and Tilly understands.
coverage.performanceFocus: Patch’s hand-to-chest honesty, Jenny’s eye contact, Tilly’s small recalibration look toward the machine.
coverage.landingImage: The walls have stopped pressing; Tilly’s attention has turned to the machine with new understanding.
coverage.cutReason: The view changes from physical holding to emotional naming; remaining on Rumble would make Patch’s turn feel secondary.

units.closingImage: The folded walls have halted around the group; Rumble remains braced, Patch kneels near Jenny’s echo, and Tilly faces the machine with new focus.

stagePlan.purpose: Begin turning the forbidden word into an object the group can handle lightly.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: Nib finds a scrap of cardboard and pencil, writes a sign reading THE BRIGGLE CAFE, proudly holds it up, Tilly stares and says, “Why?”
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: The held emotional pause tilts into odd possibility instead of another serious fix.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Cut into the paused room with Nib moving through the safe space, but keep Jenny’s echo visible so the joke’s target is clear: the word, not her.
stagePlan.observableEndState: Nib’s cafe sign is up and Tilly is staring at it.

stagePlan.purpose: Let the audience realise the mistake can be laughed with.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: Nib says, “Because if I made a mistake that good, I would sell soup from it.” A tiny silence follows, and Jenny’s echo smiles.
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: The room tests whether the laugh is safe; Jenny’s smile proves it is.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Hold the wide shared frame through the tiny silence rather than cutting to force the laugh.
stagePlan.observableEndState: Jenny’s echo smiles for the first time.

stagePlan.purpose: Have the whole group validate the play and drain the word’s power.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: Patch points at the sign and says, “I would visit.” Rumble nods: “I would order bread.” Tilly tries not to smile: “The spelling would need work.” Nib shrugs: “So would the soup.” Jenny’s echo laughs softly and the wall word shrinks.
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: Shared play becomes repair; the group laughs with the mistake and Jenny is included instead of exposed.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Let the group’s curved, low staging replace the earlier upright pressure; hold the laugh and the word shrink in one frame.
stagePlan.observableEndState: Jenny’s echo is smiling after a soft laugh while the wall word is visibly smaller.

coverage.purpose: Show Nib claiming the charged word sideways, not correcting it.
coverage.framingAndCamera: Wide frame from the safe pocket, with Nib’s scrap-and-pencil action in the lower middle and the reduced wall pressure still behind.
coverage.storyAction: Nib writes and holds up THE BRIGGLE CAFE; Tilly asks why.
coverage.performanceFocus: Nib is proud and practical in his odd logic; Tilly is genuinely baffled, not mean.
coverage.landingImage: Nib’s cafe sign faces the group while Jenny’s echo watches from the safe space.
coverage.cutReason: This is the opening after the emotional pause; a new view allows Nib’s play object to enter as a changed idea.

coverage.purpose: Protect the tiny silence where the joke becomes safe.
coverage.framingAndCamera: Same wide shared field with Nib, sign, Tilly, Patch, Rumble and Jenny’s echo all visible; no push-in to demand laughter.
coverage.storyAction: Nib explains the soup idea; silence; Jenny’s echo smiles.
coverage.performanceFocus: Nib waits without panic; Jenny’s smile is small but decisive.
coverage.landingImage: Jenny’s echo smiles while Nib’s sign remains visible.
coverage.cutReason: No cut within the silence; holding is stronger because the audience must see the joke land safely.

coverage.purpose: Let the group build the cafe game until the word loses power.
coverage.framingAndCamera: Wide, slightly warmer, with curved group staging around the sign and the wall word shrinking in the background/depth.
coverage.storyAction: Patch, Rumble, Tilly and Nib add to the cafe game; Jenny’s echo laughs softly and the word shrinks.
coverage.performanceFocus: Patch and Rumble join sincerely, Tilly allows a smile through precision, Nib buttons gently, Jenny laughs with them.
coverage.landingImage: Jenny’s echo smiles as the wall word has shrunk behind the shared play space.
coverage.cutReason: The view widens/warms because the group’s participation changes the emotional field; speaker coverage would break the shared joke.

units.closingImage: Jenny’s emotional echo smiles in the shared space while Nib’s cafe sign sits among the group and the once-dominant wall word is reduced behind them.

stagePlan.purpose: Show Tilly accepting the lesson by changing the machine’s purpose.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: Tilly looks at the Correct Answer Machine, tears off the old sign, writes a new Try Again Machine sign, and fixes it onto the device.
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: Precision returns, but now it serves gentleness rather than certainty.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Cut from Jenny’s safe laugh to Tilly’s recalibration, keeping the smiling echo and reduced word in the same room so the repair feels earned.
stagePlan.observableEndState: The machine is visibly relabelled as a Try Again Machine.

stagePlan.purpose: Make the final mechanism modest and rhythmic, not victorious.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: Patch turns the handle; the machine clunks gently; a golden card slides out and Jenny’s echo picks it up.
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: The tool is no longer an answer cannon; it has become an invitation to try again.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Hold the handle action and card slide in a calm wide frame, with the sound softened from the earlier clunking.
stagePlan.observableEndState: Jenny’s echo holds the golden card.

stagePlan.purpose: Land the room’s exhale and send the repair toward Jenny’s real life.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: The card’s message is visible, Jenny’s echo stands taller, the classroom warms, the huge wall word changes back to BRIDGE, Patch smiles and says, “There it is.” Golden repair light rises from the card and travels upward out of the shoebox world.
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: Relief arrives as a small brave lift rather than a trophy win.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Widen to rhyme with the opening classroom, now resized and warm; hold the light rising with Jenny’s taller echo and the calm word together.
stagePlan.observableEndState: Golden repair light leaves the warmed cardboard classroom.

coverage.purpose: Show Tilly’s recalibration as action, not explanation.
coverage.framingAndCamera: Wide view of the same shared room, with Tilly at the machine, Jenny’s echo still safer nearby, and the reduced wall word in depth.
coverage.storyAction: Tilly removes the old sign and writes TRY AGAIN MACHINE.
coverage.performanceFocus: Tilly’s precision slows down; she repairs the tool’s purpose instead of defending it.
coverage.landingImage: The machine carries its new sign.
coverage.cutReason: This is the opening after the play beat; the changed focus to machine transformation needs a clean editorial boundary.

coverage.purpose: Let Patch complete his arc with a gentle handle turn.
coverage.framingAndCamera: Wide-low frame around Patch at the handle, Jenny’s echo near the output slot, and Tilly giving the machine space to be used differently.
coverage.storyAction: Patch turns the handle; the machine clunks gently; a golden card slides out and Jenny’s echo picks it up.
coverage.performanceFocus: Patch’s movement is rhythmic and modest; Jenny’s echo chooses to pick up the card herself.
coverage.landingImage: Jenny’s echo holds the golden card beside the transformed machine.
coverage.cutReason: The view changes from Tilly’s relabelling to Patch’s try-again action; remaining on Tilly would misassign the emotional completion.

coverage.purpose: Deliver the opening-closing rhyme and the room’s breath returning.
coverage.framingAndCamera: Wide classroom rhyme to the opener: board, word, machine, golden card, Jenny’s taller echo and repair light all visible with warmer space above.
coverage.storyAction: Jenny’s echo stands taller; the room warms; the wall word changes to BRIDGE; Patch says the final line; repair light rises upward.
coverage.performanceFocus: Jenny’s taller stance carries the feeling; Patch’s smile is quiet recognition, not celebration.
coverage.landingImage: Golden repair light rises out of the warmed classroom above Jenny’s taller echo, the calm board word, the machine and golden card.
coverage.cutReason: The view widens because the whole room changes state; a closer reaction would weaken the exhale image.

units.closingImage: Golden repair light rises above the warmed cardboard classroom where BRIDGE sits calmly on the board, Jenny’s emotional echo stands taller near the golden card, and the transformed machine rests below.

specificContinuityRisks: Keep all six cast elements visible in the wide classroom field at the landing, including the high BRIGGLE word and Jenny’s curled echo near the board.
Do not crop bodies, the board word, Jenny’s worksheet, or the squeaking desk action.
The final eyeline must clearly move from the high word down/forward to Jenny’s emotional echo.
No one touches or crowds Jenny’s emotional echo; the respectful floor gap must remain readable.
Jenny’s worksheet grip must visibly loosen by the end.
Keep Nib’s raised-hand beat in the same wide shared frame, not isolated as a teasing punchline.
Cause and effect must read clearly: handle turn creates cards, cards/correctness coincide with Jenny shrinking and BRIGGLE enlarging.
Keep the stopped machine physically between helpers and Jenny’s echo at the landing.
Do not make Tilly smug; her stop must read as sincere recalibration after visible harm.
Rumble’s hands and sliding feet must stay visible while he holds only part of the wall open.
Patch must touch only his own chest, not Jenny’s emotional echo.
The walls must visibly stop pressing after Patch’s truth, with BRIGGLE flickering rather than vanishing.
The joke must be aimed at Nib’s cafe sign and the word, never at Jenny’s echo or her body.
Hold the tiny silence long enough for Jenny’s first smile to be visible before the ensemble joins.
The wall word must visibly shrink only after Jenny’s soft laugh, not before.
Jenny’s emotional echo must pick up and hold the golden card herself; no helper hands it to her.
The board word must resolve from BRIGGLE to BRIDGE before the final repair-light exit is complete.
End wide with MACHINE, Jenny’s taller stance, golden card, BRIDGE and rising repair light all visible.

scene.purpose: Inside Jenny’s shoebox shame classroom, the monsters discover that one wrong word has become the whole room, then change the repair from correctness to safe nearness, shared play and trying again.
scene.dramaticQuestion: Can Patch help Jenny’s emotional echo feel big enough to meet the mistake again without making the shame louder?
scene.connectionFromPreviousScene: The Fold’s call has brought the monsters into Jenny’s hidden emotional world after she hides the worksheet in her shoebox.
scene.handoverToNextScene: The room has exhaled: BRIGGLE can become BRIDGE, Jenny’s echo stands taller, and the repair light rises toward Jenny’s real morning.

beats.sourceScript: The monsters tumble into a cardboard classroom built from Jenny’s school materials, where BRIGGLE has become huge, echoing and absurdly self-important. They recognise that the feeling has built a whole room around one moment, then see Jenny’s emotional echo, small and curled inward near the board.

orderedEvents.text: Shot 07: Arrival In The Shoebox World
The Box Monsters tumble into a cardboard classroom.
Everything is handmade from folded paper, old tape and bits of schoolwork.
On the wall, huge letters loom:
The word echoes around the room.

beats.sourceScript: Patch approaches Jenny’s echo slowly and lowers himself to her level, choosing proximity without pressure. He and Nib make Patch’s own wrong word safe and funny, while Rumble adds permission not to feel big yet. Jenny’s hands loosen, showing the first small trust in the room.

beats.sourceScript: Tilly, trying to be useful, unfolds a machine designed to produce correctness. The device clunks out certainty, but Jenny’s echo shrinks and BRIGGLE grows. Rumble sees the harm, Tilly stops, and Patch realises that being correct is not the same as helping someone feel better.
exactDialogue: Tilly: Good news. I have identified the issue.
Patch: That sounds... very answer-y.
MACHINE: Correct. Correct. Correct. Correct.
Rumble: She is getting smaller.
Tilly: That was not the intended outcome.
Patch: Maybe correct is not the same as better.

beats.whoDrives: Tilly drives the action with the machine; the room drives the consequence; Rumble and Patch drive the recognition that harm is happening.

beats.actionOrChoice: Tilly unfolds and activates the Correct Answer Machine, then stops when its result visibly hurts Jenny’s echo.

emotionContract.entryState: Precise, useful and confident that identifying the issue will help.

emotionContract.choiceOrRealisation: Tilly stops the machine when Rumble names the visible harm and accepts that the outcome is wrong.
emotionContract.exitState: Recalibrating, no longer treating the feeling as a puzzle to solve by force.
emotionContract.observableEvidence: Her machine clunks certainty into the room; after Jenny’s echo shrinks, she stops and states that the outcome was not intended.
emotionContract.heldAfterBeat: Patch’s line holds the new rule: correct is not automatically better.

comedyContract.mechanism: A too-certain invention behaves like a practical answer to an emotional problem, exposing the mismatch.
comedyContract.setup: Tilly identifies the issue and produces a machine designed to output correctness.
comedyContract.expectation: A machine that says the right thing should make the classroom better.
comedyContract.disruption: Its repeated correctness makes Jenny’s echo smaller and BRIGGLE bigger.
comedyContract.button: Maybe correct is not the same as better.
comedyContract.hold: Hold after Patch’s realisation with the machine still present in the group’s space, so the audience can see the cost of the wrong help.

beats.sourceScript: The shame world tightens as the walls fold inward and the repeated word gets louder. Rumble physically holds space as best he can while Patch kneels by Jenny’s echo and names the fear beneath the mistake: feeling like everyone can see it. Then he separates the mistake from Jenny’s size, and the room pauses long enough for Tilly to understand what has to change.
exactDialogue: BRIGGLE ECHO: Briggle. Briggle. Briggle.
Rumble: I have got this.
Rumble: I have got some of this.
Patch: When I get something wrong, I feel like everyone can see it.
Patch: But getting it wrong did not make you small.

orderedEvents.text: The cardboard walls begin to fold inward.
The huge word BRIGGLE repeats louder.
Rumble presses both hands against one wall.

orderedEvents.speaker: Rumble
orderedEvents.text: I have got some of this.

orderedEvents.speaker: Patch
orderedEvents.text: When I get something wrong, I feel like everyone can see it.
Patch places a hand on his chest.

orderedEvents.speaker: Patch
orderedEvents.text: But getting it wrong did not make you small.
Tilly looks at her machine, understanding.
Final Frame: The walls stop pressing in.

beats.whoDrives: The folding room drives the crisis; Rumble holds usable space; Patch drives the emotional truth.

beats.consequence: The room pauses; Tilly can see what the machine must become, and Jenny’s echo is no longer alone inside the fear.
beats.emotionalOrComicHandover: Rumble’s understated struggle gives a small breath of comedy before Patch’s quiet truth lands.

emotionContract.entryState: Concerned, chastened by the failed machine, and now fully focused on Jenny’s echo.
emotionContract.pressure: BRIGGLE repeats louder, walls fold inward, and Rumble can only hold part of the room open.
emotionContract.choiceOrRealisation: Patch admits the visible fear of being seen through a mistake, then tells Jenny’s echo the mistake has not made her small.
emotionContract.exitState: Steady and connected, no longer trying to make the word disappear first.
emotionContract.observableEvidence: He kneels by Jenny’s echo, keeps his attention low and near, and lets the line sit as the room pauses.
emotionContract.heldAfterBeat: The emotional rule is held in silence: staying near is the repair that lets trying again become possible.

comedyContract.mechanism: Gentle understatement under physical pressure, true to Rumble’s protective nature.
comedyContract.setup: Rumble confidently braces the folding walls while the shame room presses inward.
comedyContract.expectation: His reassurance means the danger is fully contained.
comedyContract.disruption: He immediately revises the claim because the room is too much to hold completely.
comedyContract.button: I have got some of this.
comedyContract.hold: Let the small laugh pass while the walls remain visibly pressing, then settle into Patch’s quieter truth without cutting for a joke reaction.

beats.sourceScript: Nib reframes the forbidden word by making it the name of an imaginary cafe, treating the mistake as oddly valuable instead of humiliating. The others join the game with gentle sincerity, and Jenny’s echo smiles, then laughs. BRIGGLE shrinks because it is no longer only evidence against her; it has become something she can play with.
exactDialogue: Tilly: Why?
Nib: Because if I made a mistake that good, I would sell soup from it.
Patch: I would visit.
Rumble: I would order bread.
Tilly: The spelling would need work.
Nib: So would the soup.

orderedEvents.text: Nib finds a scrap of cardboard and a pencil.
He writes something, then proudly holds it up.

orderedEvents.speaker: Nib
orderedEvents.text: Because if I made a mistake that good, I would sell soup from it.
Final Frame: Jenny’s echo smiling for the first time.

beats.whatChanges: BRIGGLE changes from forbidden evidence against Jenny into a shared play object, and Jenny’s echo moves from near-smile to laughter.
beats.whoDrives: Nib drives the reframing; Patch, Rumble and Tilly validate it by joining sincerely rather than explaining it.
beats.audienceAnticipation: The audience waits to see if laughing with the mistake will feel safe for Jenny’s echo, not like laughing at her.
beats.actionOrChoice: Nib spatially takes over the shame word as an imaginary cafe sign, and the others gently accept the game.
beats.consequence: Jenny’s echo smiles and laughs; BRIGGLE shrinks because it no longer controls the whole room’s meaning.
beats.emotionalOrComicHandover: Shared play releases the pressure and hands the scene to practical repair.

emotionContract.entryState: Curious and ready to treat the wrong word sideways rather than as a problem to erase.
emotionContract.pressure: BRIGGLE has been too loud to say safely, and Jenny’s echo has only just begun to trust the room.
emotionContract.choiceOrRealisation: Nib treats the mistake as oddly valuable and usable, without mocking Jenny.
emotionContract.exitState: Delighted but gentle, having helped the group laugh with the word instead of at the child.
emotionContract.observableEvidence: He reframes BRIGGLE as a cafe, the others join, Jenny’s echo smiles then laughs, and the word shrinks.
emotionContract.heldAfterBeat: The audience holds relief: the mistake can be played with and survived.

comedyContract.mechanism: A forbidden shame word is spatially reclaimed as an imaginary cafe, turning evidence into play through Nib’s odd logic.
comedyContract.setup: Patch has named the fear, the room has paused, and BRIGGLE remains charged with embarrassment.
comedyContract.expectation: The next step should be a careful correction or another repair tool.
comedyContract.disruption: Nib treats BRIGGLE as such a good mistake that it could sell soup, and the others join the pretend business with full sincerity.
comedyContract.hold: Do not rush off the laugh; hold wide enough to see Jenny’s echo smiling and BRIGGLE reduced in power before moving to the repair.

physicalStaging.staysVisible: BRIGGLE, Jenny’s echo, Nib’s cafe takeover space, and the supporting monsters stay in the same wide emotional field so the audience can track that the joke is shared safely.
physicalStaging.contactAndWeight: Nib handles only classroom materials and the word’s play space; no grabbing Jenny’s echo. Any shifted desks, signs or makeshift counter pieces keep cardboard weight and settle before the next line.
physicalStaging.payoffShape: The accusing upright word becomes a usable cafe sign/menu/counter shape, then visibly shrinks as Jenny’s echo laughs.
prohibitedStaging: Do not stage the group pointing at Jenny’s echo while joking.
Do not let props or letters topple onto Jenny’s echo for slapstick.
Do not cut away from Jenny’s near-smile and laugh before the audience sees the joke is safe.

beats.sourceScript: Tilly accepts the lesson and transforms the Correct Answer Machine into a Try Again Machine. Patch turns the handle, and a golden card gives Jenny’s echo the truth of the episode. She stands taller, the classroom warms, BRIGGLE becomes BRIDGE, and the repair light rises out of the shoebox world toward Jenny’s real life.
exactDialogue: Patch: There it is.

orderedEvents.text: Tilly looks at the Correct Answer Machine.
Then she writes a new one:
WRONG IS NOT THE SAME AS SMALL
The huge word on the wall changes from BRIGGLE to BRIDGE.
The golden repair light rises from the card and travels upward, out of the shoebox world.
Final Frame: Golden repair light leaving the cardboard classroom.

beats.whatChanges: The machine changes purpose, the word changes back, and Jenny’s echo stands taller inside the same room that previously made her small.
beats.whoDrives: Tilly drives the practical transformation; Patch completes the emotional turn by using the machine modestly as a Try Again action.
beats.audienceAnticipation: The audience expects the repair to be gentle and earned, not a loud victory over BRIGGLE.
beats.actionOrChoice: Tilly transforms the Correct Answer Machine into a Try Again Machine, and Patch turns the handle with a rhythmic, modest motion.
beats.consequence: A golden card appears, Jenny’s echo stands taller, the room warms, BRIGGLE becomes BRIDGE, and repair light rises toward Jenny’s real life.
beats.emotionalOrComicHandover: The scene hands over to morning with relief rather than triumph: the feeling is carryable now.

emotionContract.entryState: Steady, having learned that safety and play must come before correction.
emotionContract.pressure: The room still contains the machine and the word, so the final repair must not undo the lesson by becoming hard certainty again.
emotionContract.choiceOrRealisation: Patch turns the handle as a try-again action, not as a conquest, accepting that the mistake can be met safely.
emotionContract.exitState: Quietly relieved and braver in stillness than he was in urgency.
emotionContract.observableEvidence: He uses the transformed machine gently; Jenny’s echo stands taller as BRIGGLE settles into BRIDGE and warm repair light rises.
emotionContract.heldAfterBeat: Relief with a small brave lift: Jenny’s shame has not been erased, but it is no longer bigger than her.

comedyContract.mechanism: No comic mechanism; the rhythm is emotional release and modest repair.
comedyContract.setup: The wrong repair machine remains in the room after BRIGGLE has been made safe through play.
comedyContract.expectation: A final device action might become a triumphant fix.
comedyContract.disruption: The handle turn is small and rhythmic, letting the room exhale rather than celebrate loudly.
comedyContract.hold: Hold the warmed classroom, Jenny’s taller echo, BRIDGE, golden card and rising repair light together so the audience can feel the breath return.

shots.physicalPerformance: Tilly returns to the machine with slower, humbler precision: old label off, new purpose written and fixed on. Patch takes the handle without flourish and turns it in a gentle rhythm. The device releases a golden card, which Jenny’s echo chooses to pick up herself. She stands taller as the room warms and the board lettering settles into the intended classroom word. Patch’s smile is small recognition, and the repair light rises upward out of the room.
shots.animationTiming: Keep the relabel calm and practical, the handle turn steady and softened, and the card pickup unhurried. Hold Jenny’s taller stance and the room-wide warming before letting the repair light rise and linger.

performanceContract.playableIntention: Patch completes his turn by using the transformed machine as an invitation, while Tilly makes the tool serve gentleness and Jenny’s echo carries the final change herself.

phases.observableAction: Tilly faces the stopped machine, removes its old label, writes a new label, and fixes it onto the device with careful hands.
Patch turns the handle with a small steady motion as the machine gives a softer clunk and releases a golden card.

performanceContract.physicalCauseAndEffect: Tilly’s relabelling changes the device’s function; Patch’s gentle handle turn activates it without the earlier harsh output; the card reaches Jenny’s echo; her self-directed pickup and taller stance trigger the room warming, the board word resolving, and the repair light leaving upward.
performanceContract.visibleEmotionalTurn: The machine changes from intrusive pressure to modest support, and Jenny’s echo changes from protected participant to the figure holding the repair card and standing taller.

characterTruths.pressureResponse: She corrects the machine’s purpose quietly, without defending the earlier failure.

characterTruths.canonTrait: Brave, warm first responder who learns by staying with the feeling.

showrunnerJudgement: Pass. I tried to break this scene on the usual failure points — classroom line-up staging, speaker-by-speaker reaction coverage, decorative feelings, machine-as-gag, and a triumphal repair — but the storyboard holds the governing experience. The scene accumulates behaviour rather than announcing emotion: Patch’s body changes from arrival momentum to low nearness; Jenny’s echo changes through hands, gaze, smile, laugh and height; Rumble physically makes space; Tilly’s precision visibly harms and then recalibrates; Nib’s play changes the audience’s laugh from nervous to shared. At least one major beat remains legible without sound: Rumble bracing the folding wall while Patch kneels with Jenny’s echo clearly carries the danger, relationship distance and emotional turn in staging alone. The camera stays wide and emotionally present rather than cutting to every line, and the word remains an environmental weight rather than becoming a fight-monster.
